title: Fix Procedural 3D Sphere-Cut-Torus Infinite Hang
description: In the procedural-3d dev app (bun run dev:procedural:3d, port 6018), selecting a "sphere cut with torus" boolean operation in the catalogue/workbench causes the UI to hang indefinitely (browser tab becomes unresponsive, no error surfaces). Need to reproduce, find the root cause (likely in the BRep boolean/cut kernel or the procedural plugin's evaluation of a sphere-torus difference), and fix the hang without introducing legacy/compat shims. Repo is greenfield; refactor cleanly at the root cause.
summary:
Investigated the reported "infinite hang" when selecting the Sphere Cut With Torus procedural-3d example. Reproduced it live in-browser multiple times (WebGL context lost, main JS thread verified fully blocked — even a trivial `1+1` eval via CDP timed out).

Root-caused via isolated testing outside the flaky shared dev server, since it wouldn't help attribute cause given heavy concurrent unrelated activity on this machine (load avg 40-46, other dev/build processes, a shared plugin registry file getting clobbered by other concurrently-running `bun script.ts dev <plugin>` processes, and the vite dev server itself churning from unrelated concurrent file edits):

1. Native Rust test of the exact fixture params (sphere r=2.2, torus 2.0/0.5, cut) completes correctly in 1.3s — no logic bug, no infinite loop.
2. All 25 existing procedural-plugin tests pass, including the cache-preservation and sphere-cut-torus-specific tests already added in the prior #1878 fix.
3. Installed wasmtime and ran the same test under the actual wasm32-wasip2 target (matching the browser's real target) — also completes correctly, but in ~20s, ~15x slower than native. This is the real culprit: not an infinite loop, but a synchronous, main-thread-blocking computation that is slow enough in wasm (and far worse under this machine's current CPU contention) to look and feel like a permanent hang, including tripping the browser's WebGL-hang detection.
4. Found the cost concentrated in `boolean_mesh_sync`'s internal tessellation deflection (0.03) used to prep the sphere/torus for the CDT-based mesh-boolean when a torus surface is involved — this is prep-only resolution (not the final render mesh), so it can be much coarser. Coarsened it to 0.1 in kernel/3d/brep/rs/lib.rs; re-ran the same wasm32 test: 6.34s, a ~3.2x improvement, with the full native suite (all 15 kernel tests) still passing including volume/triangle-count accuracy assertions.

This is a genuine, verified, safe performance fix, not a full elimination of the multi-second synchronous stall. The deeper architectural fix — running plugin WASM evaluation off the main thread (e.g. a Web Worker) so a slow CSG op doesn't freeze the tab — is out of scope for this ticket and flagged as a follow-up, not attempted here to avoid a half-finished cross-cutting change to the plugin host architecture.

Also fixed, as a byproduct of testing: repeatedly regenerated the shared framework/plugin/registry/generated/plugins.ts (via `bun framework/plugin/registry/script.ts generate procedural`) each time a concurrent dev process clobbered it — no code change, just documenting that this shared last-writer-wins registry file is a known source of "No plugins loaded" boot failures when multiple `dev <plugin>` targets run concurrently (same root cause noted in the earlier VCS-COMMAND-ARCHITECTURE session).
